questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: Practice my mandarin and travel to a place I have never been to before.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That it was a mandarin-speaking country.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was really amazing!!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy to find on the website, and if it was troublesome, you could always write an email or call the international contact at NTU.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Unfortunately my assigned student volunteer did not contact me, but my danish classmates from KU who also came to NTU had a very good student volunteer we could ask for help. And fortunately I had a Taiwanese friend who was a NTU student, which I asked for help.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was a nice orientation that provided a lot of information in an engaging way.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy to find expensive housing and hard to find local cheaper housing. Luckily, I had a friend who helped me find housing 10 min in bus from campus to a decent price, but I only managed that because of the help. So I recommend looking for recommendation at least 2 months before, maybe 3 months before, and if possible look at the local websites even though it is in Chinese.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's a great way to experience a more local way of living. I personally enjoyed that! It as a bit daunting to sign a contract written in traditional characters, but it will all work out in the end, and I was lucky to have a nice landlord and a helpful housemate. My advice is to don't be shy to ask for help and ask questions when in doubt! The Taiwanese are very friendly and helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The reason why I'm not satisfied is because there was not enough dorms, originally I had hoped to live at the dorms. There was actually space at the dorms further away, but I do not recommend living there, they are 40 min from campus, which I personally would hate.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It's fairly long, and use your classmates when in doubt. We had a group chat with the KU students going to NTU.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Stressfull and long. So many emails. But you will get through it. Use your KU classmates for help and support. They make it seem more urgent and strict than it really is.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The international contact at NTU, but mostly I used my classmates and the local NTU student that I new. Hopefully you can use your student volunteer.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was fairly succesfull! But I think I was lucky, and I applied for a lot of courses (around 18 courses I think).

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Talk with your classmates about courses, because NTU have a huge amount of courses and it's hard to choose. Talk with other internationals during and before orientation to get inspired. Don't hold back trying new courses. Don't be too quick to settle.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was satisfied. Of course some teachers were better than others, but I enjoyed most of my classes.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had taken mandarin courses and marketing courses. The marketing courses was very introductory, so they were fairly easy and manageable. The mandarin courses were definitely the most demanding, so I don't recommend the mandarin courses if your motive for going abroad is to relax and have fun.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I didn't find that big of a difference in teaching style, however the grading system is very different.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Enhancing Chinese, general Chinese, ICL International Companions for Learning, Engaging Consumers and Social Media Marketing, Global Marketing and Negotiations Skills, Green Marketing, Exploring Taiwan: Women and Taiwanese Society.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you want to learn Mandarin or improve your mandarin, I recommend the mandarin courses. The marketing courses were very introductory so if you already have knowledge within this area I would not recommend it, unless you just want to relax. I especially enjoyed Engaging Consumers and Social Media Marketing, because the teacher was very nice and engaging.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Even though taxa is very cheap compared to Denmark, it can quickly add up, because public transport closes around midnight. So if possible, use the UBike, if you want to save money. Going to cafe almost everyday also adds up. Alcohol is surprisingly expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Taxa was cheap and food was very cheap. Public transport was very cheap. Alcohol and phone subscription were surprisingly expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I joined the hiking club which was a very nice way to meet local NTU students, so I highly recommend joining a club!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a lot of activities available, I recommend going to the club fair in the beginning of the semester!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join a club if you want to meet local students!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel around Taiwan, there are wonderful nature and cities to explore! Taipei is also amazing and have a ton of things to see and do, both nature stuff and city stuff!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy, but I am also used to asian culture. Everyone are very nice and friendly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a club!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The garbage truck! But that is only a problem if you don't live at a dorm.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The amazing food, nature and people!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Use your KU classmates during the registration period before arriving. Join a club at NTU. Try and enjoy and relax, everything works out in the end.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't hold back to ask for help if needed! Enjoy and have fun!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To experience living in another country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To make local friends, because internationals and your fellow KU students are so much easier to talk to.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
